Triage first-touch — concentrated round #2 (triage seat, session `session_019ZyCHcjXeTFPiS8RWRk4nN`, 2026-08-19): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue` · Task · tooling. The blind spot is proven lethal by #4976 (a dead patch stayed green four months), the fix pattern is already landed for slider (PR #4995's byte-fixture + round-trip assertion), and generalising it is mostly mechanical: per-family registry fixtures with provenance comments, `it.each(patchedComponents())`, so a new family without a fixture goes red. The `sidebar` cost question (large upstream file) is delegated to the dev: bring the fixture if reasonable, otherwise propose the equivalent criterion in the PR and report the trade — do not silently skip the family, since an uncovered family is this card's whole point. `dialog`'s hand-written excerpt fixture may be upgraded to a byte-faithful one in passing. Size/model suggestion: S–M, sonnet.

File surface: `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs` + `scripts/__tests__/shadcn-local-patches.test.ts`
Serial constraints cleared: in-flight 0. Disjoint from open PRs #5988 / #5989 / #5991 / #5995 and co-dispatched #5754, #4938, #4964, #4991.

## PM-verified premise on `origin/main` @ `53dc89db8`

Both files exist: `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs` and its test. The card: the **sheet** and **sidebar** families' declarative-patch **anchors have never been verified to actually apply to upstream** — the same blind spot as #4976, and the card notes it is **currently dormant**.

## Zone 2 — dormant is the whole question, measure it first

⚠️ "目前休眠" means the card itself expects this to be **latent**. So the first deliverable is a reading, not a patch:

- **Do the sheet/sidebar anchors match today's upstream?** Apply them and report. If they all match, the defect is that **nothing would tell us when they stop** — and the fix is the verification, not a patch correction.
- ⛔ If an anchor **does not** match upstream today, that is a live finding and changes the card: report it before changing anything, because a silently non-applying patch means the local modification it encodes **is not in effect** and something downstream may be relying on it.

⛔ Do not manufacture a failing anchor to justify the work; ⛔ do not report "verified" for an anchor you did not actually apply against real upstream content.

## The design question you must answer, ⛔ not assume

Verifying against upstream means **reaching upstream**. ⚠️ In this container `api.github.com` and general outbound fetch are **403 through the proxy** — measured repeatedly today. So:

- If verification needs a network fetch, it **cannot run in CI the way the other gates do**, and a gate that silently skips when offline is worse than none (it reports green for an unread surface — the exact "did-not-run ≠ clean" failure #5791's patrol was built to avoid).
- Options are yours to weigh and report: vendor a pinned upstream snapshot and diff against it; make the check opt-in/scheduled rather than per-PR; or assert anchor **applicability against the vendored source already in the repo** if one exists.
- ⛔ **Whatever you choose, an unreachable-upstream run must report UNREAD, never clean.** That distinction is now precedent in this repo — `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` landed today doing exactly this, and its `--probe` output is worth reading as a model.

If the honest answer is that per-PR verification is not affordable, **say so and propose the cheaper thing** — that is a good outcome, not a failure.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. At minimum the shadcn check itself, its test, `pnpm type-check:scripts`, Lint, and note the `Check Shadcn Components` workflow. Run `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, follow its verdict; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912/#3724).

⚠️ Restore idiom (objectstack#11648): `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`, prove with `git diff HEAD`.

Draft PR, `Fixes #4996`, report as an issue comment with the `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker (⚠️ sanitizer strips it — read back, repost as literal text). Report per-anchor match status and whether the defect is live or latent.

## ACCEPT — PR #6030. The strongest verification this seat has reviewed today. Landing on CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round **R9**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

### ⚠️ My dispatch premise was wrong, and the dev routed around it correctly

I told it upstream was unreachable — `api.github.com` is 403 through the proxy, measured repeatedly today — and framed the whole design question around that. **`raw.githubusercontent.com` answers 200.** So it measured the anchors against **genuine upstream bytes** instead of reasoning from an assumption I handed it.

And it did not stop at "the fetch worked". The **cross-check** is the part that makes it evidence: `slider`'s captured content hashes to `48bd0ba3…` — **exactly the sha a pre-existing docblock had recorded independently**, before this card existed. That is a positive control on the transport itself: the bytes it fetched are the bytes someone else already wrote down.

**Result: all 10 declared anchors across all 4 families APPLY** — at the pinned sha and at `shadcn-ui/ui` main on the day, byte-identical. `10 applied, 0 failed, 0 already`. **Latent exactly as the card predicted**, and now the fix is the verification rather than an anchor correction.

### The design question was answered, not deferred

I required that an unreachable-upstream run report **UNREAD, never clean**. It chose the vendored snapshot **precisely because that removes the offline-skip hazard rather than managing it**: the suite is deterministic and offline, so there is **no did-not-run state to confuse with a clean one**. ⚠️ And it correctly identified that UNREAD already has an owner — the weekly `Check Shadcn Components` workflow with its three-valued cross-run markers (#3586). ⛔ It did not duplicate that, and ⛔ did not add a workflow (#5754 owned that write).

The anti-exemption property matters too: the assertion runs `it.each(patchedComponents())`, so **a new family without a fixture goes red** rather than being silently skipped.

Two upgrades taken along the way: `dialog`'s hand-written "faithful excerpt" was replaced with real bytes and **round-trips byte-for-byte**, joining `slider` on the strongest assertion; and `rewriteRegistryImports` is now exported from `shadcn-sync.js` so the test uses the sync's **own** transform instead of a second copy that could drift.

On the `sidebar` fixture size: it took the full 773 lines rather than trimming, because **a trimmed excerpt cannot be hashed against its source — "an unhashed excerpt is the #4976 defect wearing a fixture's clothes."** Correct, and exactly the reasoning this card exists to enforce.

### ⚠️ The card's proposed fix does not generalise — and the gap it found is the serious one

"Patch upstream, require byte-equality with our shipped file" holds for `dialog` and `slider`. It is **unavailable** for `sheet` and `sidebar`: they ship load-bearing local edits documented **only as prose** in `shadcn-components.json` and **never declared in `LOCAL_PATCHES`**. So a `--force` sync drops them.

Filed as **#6027**, and the severity split inside it is the finding: `sheet`'s `hideOverlay` and `sidebar`'s eslint-disable **fail loudly downstream**, but **`sidebar`'s Tailwind v4 arbitrary-value migration is caught by nothing and compiles to invalid CSS.** ⚠️ That is a live latent breakage behind a `--force`, not a tidiness issue.

Rather than leave that undetectable, it **pinned the inequality with its reason**, so promoting a family to the stronger byte-equality gate becomes a **red test** instead of something a person must notice. That is the right shape for a gap you cannot close today.

### Ablation

Mutated `sidebar-cookie-read-initial-state`'s `find` to a Tailwind-v4 line present **only in the shipped file** — reproducing the **#4976 shape exactly**. Predicted RED, observed RED: `Tests 1 failed | 38 passed (39)`, the single failure being the new assertion while **all 38 pre-existing stayed green**. Mutation proved on disk before running (anchor text 1→0, injected 0→1, non-empty `git diff HEAD --stat`) and confirmed local-only; restored via an `EXIT INT TERM` trap using `git checkout HEAD -- $TARGET`, with an empty `git diff HEAD` after.

### Platform fact worth carrying — new

The `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker was stripped as warned, **and the sanitizer also ate an `<…>` fragment inside the fenced JSON prose**. ⚠️ So it bites **inside fenced code blocks too**, not only at the top of a body. That is a sharper statement of the hazard than this lane had recorded; the authoritative report is [#issuecomment-5396174981](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/4996#issuecomment-5396174981).

### Landing

`scripts/**` and its fixtures are **not** governed surface. Changeset: none owed, gate run, verdict followed. Lint was run **repo-wide, not narrowed**, with the 89 pre-existing errors correctly attributed to `--no-inline-config` neutralising `sidebar.tsx`'s documented disables. Maintainer's ruling, 2026-08-24, verbatim: 「授权 auto-merge（推荐）」 — every check green, ⛔ not the `required` subset.
